additions.reason: The Rebbe opens: 'there are very great elevated children (בְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה) who give birth to souls above the sixty myriads.' These elevated children are then explicitly identified — 'וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת בְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה' — as the bechina/aspect of the children of Moses. They are not cause-and-effect of something else; they ARE the same thing as the children of Moses. This is node 1 of the core bechina pair in this Torah. It belongs in the single package of transcendent souls/elevated children of Moses.
additions.source_quote: אֲבָל יֵשׁ בְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה גְּדוֹלִים מְאֹד, שֶׁמּוֹלִידִים נְשָׁמוֹת שֶׁהֵם לְמַעְלָה מֵהַנְּשָׁמוֹת הַמִּתְלַבְּשִׁים בַּבָּנִים הַנּוֹלָדִים בָּעוֹלָם

additions.reason: The core identifying node. The text uses the word 'בְּחִינוֹת' explicitly: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת בְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה.' The elevated children who beget transcendent souls ARE (= share the same essential nature as) the children of Moses. This is the dominant node — it is the named archetype that gives the entire teaching its anchor. The children of Moses are defined by Chazal (Berakhot 7) as 'above sixty myriads,' meaning they transcend the standard framework of embodied souls entirely.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת בְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהֶם: וּבְנֵי רְחַבְיָה רַבּוּ לְמַעְלָה

additions.reason: The souls begotten by the elevated children are described as entirely transcending the sixty myriads — 'they are not counted from this world at all.' These transcendent souls ARE the bechina of what the children of Moses represent. The teaching identifies the quality 'above sixty myriads' (לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא) as the shared nature that unites the elevated children, the children of Moses, and the children of Rechabiah. This is the third node of the core cluster.
additions.source_quote: אֵלּוּ הַנְּשָׁמוֹת הַנַּ"ל הֵם לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נְשָׁמוֹת שֶׁמִּתְלַבְּשִׁים בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם, כִּי הֵם אֵינָם רְאוּיִין כְּלָל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם

additions.reason: The Rebbe cites 'וּבְנֵי רְחַבְיָה רַבּוּ לְמַעְלָה' as the scriptural proof-text for the children of Moses, and the Gemara (Berakhot 7) interprets 'לְמַעְלָה' as 'above sixty myriads.' The children of Rechabiah are thus identified as a bechina of the children of Moses — they ARE the exemplar case of souls that transcend the sixty-myriads framework. This is a fourth node in the same bechina cluster.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת בְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהֶם: וּבְנֵי רְחַבְיָה רַבּוּ לְמַעְלָה, וְדָרְשׁוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (ברכות ז): לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא

analysis_notes.teaching_summary: Torah #273 is a compact teaching about a category of transcendent souls: the 'elevated children' (בְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה) who beget souls that stand above the sixty-myriads framework of embodied existence. The Rebbe identifies this as the bechina of the children of Moses, citing the aggadic reading of Rechabiah's children as 'above sixty myriads.' The teaching has no explicit evil mirror — it presents a single positive domain: the transcendence of the ordinary soul-framework. There are no eitza statements; the teaching is purely a definitional/bechina equation.
